title: Shifting red lines
summary: Between 2024 and 2026 most frontier labs dropped blanket bans on military use and loosened or restructured their safety frameworks, often without announcing it. Some tightened in other areas, and Anthropic was blacklisted by the Pentagon for keeping two limits.
definition: Changes to the public limits AI labs set on themselves: usage-policy bans (weapons, military use, surveillance), international commitments, and safety frameworks that say when a lab will stop or add safeguards.
development: In 2024 most frontier labs still banned military use and had just promised, at the Seoul summit, to halt if risks passed set thresholds. Between 2024 and 2026 OpenAI, Meta, Google and Anthropic opened their models to defense and intelligence work, and several frameworks swapped binding if-then commitments for goals or competitor-contingent clauses. Changes also ran the other way, with new manipulation and loss-of-control categories, and Anthropic was blacklisted by the Pentagon in 2026 for keeping limits on autonomous weapons and domestic surveillance.
methods: Tracked by diffing archived policy pages (Midas Watchtower, Wayback Machine) and by expert scorecards (FLI, SaferAI). Diffs catch wording changes but not how policies are applied in practice, and scorecards rest on panel judgement.

chart.reason: Policy changes are not a measurable benchmark. A possible future chart: count of disclosed vs. undisclosed framework changes per year (e.g. from Midas Watchtower or the 'Silent Revision' dataset).

entries.title: OpenAI removes "military and warfare" from its usage-policy ban list
entries.quote: develop or use weapons, injure others or destroy property
entries.note: The 10 Jan 2024 rewrite dropped "Military and warfare" from the high-risk activities list (present in the Dec 2023 version) while keeping a ban on weapons; first reported by The Intercept.

entries.title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments (AI Seoul Summit)
entries.quote: organisations commit not to develop or deploy a model or system at all
entries.note: The baseline: signatories promised to publish intolerable-risk thresholds and to halt if risks could not be kept below them. Later framework changes are measured against this.

entries.title: Expanding access to Claude for government
entries.quote: we have crafted a set of contractual exceptions to our general Usage Policy
entries.note: Allowed selected agencies to use Claude for legally authorised foreign intelligence analysis; weapons, disinformation, censorship and malicious cyber uses stayed banned.

entries.title: Announcing our updated Responsible Scaling Policy (v2.0)
entries.note: Moved to capability thresholds paired with required safeguards and added flexibility after Anthropic found it had fallen short of some v1 procedural requirements.

entries.title: Open Source AI Can Help America Lead in AI and Strengthen Global Security
entries.quote: We're making Llama available to U.S. government agencies and contractors working on national security applications.
entries.note: An exception to Llama's acceptable-use ban on military uses, with defense partners including Lockheed Martin, Anduril and Palantir.

entries.title: Anthropic and Palantir partner to bring Claude to AWS for U.S. intelligence and defense
entries.note: Claude 3 and 3.5 deployed in Palantir's IL6 (up to Secret) environment. Press release could not be loaded; date and details from search excerpts and coverage.

entries.title: Google removes "applications we will not pursue" from its AI Principles
entries.quote: democracies should lead in AI development
entries.note: The rewrite dropped the pledge not to build weapons or surveillance violating international norms (still present in a 30 Jan 2025 archive of the principles page).

entries.title: Meta releases its Frontier AI Framework
entries.note: Meta's first framework under the Seoul commitments; Midas noted it gave no specific mitigations tied to its capability evaluations.

entries.title: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy v2.1
entries.note: Refined CBRN and AI R&D thresholds and dropped a pledge to define next-level evaluations before developing models at the current level (per Midas diff).

entries.title: Our updated Preparedness Framework (v2)
entries.quote: If another frontier AI developer releases a high-risk system without comparable safeguards, we may adjust our requirements.
entries.note: Made safeguards explicitly contingent on competitors and moved persuasion out of the framework.

entries.title: Strengthening our Frontier Safety Framework (v3)
entries.quote: misaligned AI models might interfere with operators’ ability to direct, modify or shut down their operations
entries.note: A tightening: added a harmful-manipulation capability level and protocols for shutdown-resistance and other misalignment risks.

entries.title: Responsible Scaling Policy v3.0
entries.quote: Rather than being hard commitments, these are public goals that we will openly grade our progress towards.
entries.note: Replaced the if-then structure (threshold reached → safeguards mandatory) with nonbinding roadmap goals and industry-wide recommendations; Midas called it the revocation of a core RSP component.

entries.title: Statement on the comments from Secretary of War Pete Hegseth
entries.quote: the mass domestic surveillance of Americans and fully autonomous weapons
entries.note: Anthropic refused to drop these two exceptions and was designated a supply-chain risk (confirmed by letter on 4 Mar 2026), a label previously reserved for foreign adversaries.

entries.title: Our agreement with the Department of War
entries.quote: No use of OpenAI technology to direct autonomous weapons systems.
entries.note: Signed the day after Anthropic's blacklisting for classified deployments, with three stated red lines; tightened on 2 Mar 2026 to bar domestic surveillance of U.S. persons explicitly.

entries.title: Where things stand with the Department of War
entries.quote: we see no choice but to challenge it in court
entries.note: Anthropic sued; Judge Rita Lin (N.D. Cal.) found the designation unlawful in Aug 2026, but the D.C. Circuit upheld a parallel designation 2–1 on 25 Sep 2026.

entries.title: Meta Advanced AI Scaling Framework v2
entries.note: Largely a tightening: added a Loss of Control domain, a lower "substantially contribute" trigger and whistleblower protections, while relabelling tiers from "Stop development" to "Develop with mitigations".

entries.title: xAI rewrites and shortens its Frontier AI Framework
entries.quote: The new FAIF removes the two quantitative risk acceptance criteria the framework contained.
entries.note: Version effective 30 Jun 2026 (found by Midas on 11 Jul) also removed whistleblower-protection language and SB 53 references, without announcement.

entries.title: AI Safety Index — Summer 2026
entries.quote: Even industry leaders in safety practices are retreating from prior commitments.
entries.note: Expert panel found Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Meta weakened or voided pause pledges and reversed earlier military-use bans between 2024 and 2026.

entries.title: Silent Revision: Measuring Undisclosed Change in the Safety Frameworks of Frontier AI Developers
entries.quote: 67% of material changes (95% CI 62 to 72) are silent under a strict standard.
entries.note: First systematic measurement of how often labs change their safety frameworks without saying so.

entries.title: D.C. Circuit upholds Pentagon supply-chain-risk designation of Anthropic
entries.note: 2–1 ruling (Henderson dissenting); a separate district-court ruling against the government remains in effect. News coverage, not the opinion itself.
